ethics.title: What we
ethics.subtitle: We're building a tool that touches people's emotional lives. This page is our explicit positioning — AI, data, dependency, clinical limits, responsibility. No fine print.
ethics.ctaNote: If anything we do doesn't match what you read here, it's a bug. Tell us.

ia.title: About artificial intelligence
ia.lead: AI is a tool, not a therapist. Our mentor uses generative models to accompany you, not to diagnose or decide for you.
ia.commit1: The mentor is built on a hardcoded pedagogical framework. It doesn't improvise: it follows a supervised process.
ia.commit2: There are automatic validators that block responses violating our principles (empty imperatives, validation without context, quick congratulations).
ia.commit3: When the AI gets it wrong, we fix the prompt and document it in the public changelog.
ia.commit4: The final decision is always yours. The mentor returns questions, not verdicts.
ia.never1: We will never use your conversations to train third-party models.
ia.never2: We will never generate clinical diagnoses or medical recommendations.
ia.never3: We will never pretend the mentor is human.

datos.title: About your data
datos.lead: What you write to the mentor is intimate. We treat it with the same care we'd expect if it were ours.
datos.commit1: Your conversations are stored encrypted and used only to give you continuity: the mentor remembers your context to accompany you better.
datos.commit2: We would only access a specific conversation if you open a support ticket and explicitly ask us to.
datos.commit3: You can export everything we have about you from settings. You can delete it. Deletion is real, not just a flag.
datos.commit4: We comply with GDPR. Servers in the European Union.
datos.never1: We will never sell your data.
datos.never2: We will never share it with advertisers or ad networks.
datos.never3: We will never cross-reference it with commercial profiles to segment you.

dependencia.title: About emotional dependency
dependencia.lead: The mentor's goal is for you to need us less, not more. We write that in code, not just marketing.
dependencia.commit1: The mentor closes every conversation leaving you with clarity, not with a need to return.
dependencia.commit2: If we detect compulsive use (many long conversations a day, no progress), the system suggests a pause and rest — not more sessions.
dependencia.commit3: We don't use addictive design patterns: no infinite scroll, no notifications to recapture attention, no variable rewards.
dependencia.commit4: Reminders are contextual and useful, not retention hooks.
dependencia.never1: We will never optimize engagement metrics at the cost of your wellbeing.
dependencia.never2: We will never add gamification mechanics designed to make you come back for the sake of coming back.
dependencia.never3: We will never say "I miss you" or similar to force reactivation.

limitesClinicos.title: About clinical limits
limitesClinicos.lead: There's a clear line between accompaniment and professional care. We don't cross it, and we make sure it doesn't cross itself.
limitesClinicos.commit1: There's a licensed clinical psychologist responsible for clinical judgment: she reviews risk detection, interventions, and the mentor's templates.
limitesClinicos.commit2: If we detect risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm, acute crisis), the mentor stops coaching and connects you with emergency resources.
limitesClinicos.commit3: We have a documented crisis protocol. The responsible psychologist signs off on every change that could affect clinical judgment.
limitesClinicos.commit4: We are a complement to therapy, not a substitute. If someone is in treatment, the human professional leads the case.
limitesClinicos.never1: We will never make psychopathological diagnoses.
limitesClinicos.never2: We will never prescribe medication or dosages.
limitesClinicos.never3: We will never discourage anyone from seeing a human professional.

responsabilidad.title: About our responsibility
responsabilidad.lead: When you build something that touches people's emotional lives, the responsibility is serious. We don't delegate it.
responsabilidad.commit1: We review conversations in aggregated and anonymized form to improve the pedagogical framework.
responsabilidad.commit2: We document every relevant change in a public changelog you can read.
responsabilidad.commit3: If you find something that violates these principles, write to us. We fix it and we publish it.
responsabilidad.commit4: We don't use minors on our platform without consent from legal guardians and additional protection mechanisms.

about.title: Every heartbeat is a
about.subtitle: Three Billion Heartbeats is born from one conviction: technology can accompany without replacing what's human. We're not a productivity app. We're a space where artificial intelligence serves what matters most — that you understand what's happening and act accordingly.
about.questionTitle: The question that started it all
about.questionP1: The human heart beats approximately three billion times in a lifetime. Each of those beats is an opportunity — to move forward, to pause, to choose.
about.questionP2: Most people know something needs to change. They feel it. But between knowing and doing there's an abyss: blockages that go unnamed, patterns that repeat, decisions that get postponed. And in that space, clarity is lost.
about.questionP3: exists to close that abyss. Not with generic advice or empty motivation, but with a question at the right moment, a mirror showing what you're not seeing, and a next step you can take today.

interpelar.title: Question before instructing
interpelar.desc: We don't tell you what to do. We ask, so you discover what you already know but don't dare to see.

porque.title: Always the why
porque.desc: Every action has a reason. Without understanding the why, action is obedience, not change.

gafas.title: New glasses
gafas.desc: We help you see what you've normalized. What you take for granted is often what holds you back the most.

localGlobal.title: From local to global
localGlobal.desc: We start with the concrete of today — your blockage, your emotion — and from there we discover the bigger pattern.

inside.title: Change comes from within
inside.desc: It isn't imposed. It's questioned into being. The right question creates more change than the best instruction.

progress.title: Progress, not perfection
progress.desc: An imperfect step today is worth more than a perfect plan tomorrow. Moving forward is what counts.

startidea.p2Pre: After 15 years watching how people get stuck, postpone, and lose clarity — even when they have resources and motivation — we asked ourselves:
startidea.p2Strong: what if technology could do what a good mentor does? Be there, at the right moment, with the right question.

A project that combines artificial intelligence, behavioral psychology, and 15 years of real-world accompaniment experience to create something that didn't exist: a mentor that doesn't give answers — it asks the questions you're not asking yourself.

founder.name: Mario Pablo Sánchez Barrón
founder.role: Founder of Startidea · Creator of Three Billion Heartbeats
founder.p1: With over 15 years of experience developing digital products with social impact, Mario has combined technology with a deeply human vision: digital tools should help people understand themselves better and act accordingly.
founder.p2: After years working with teams, clients, and organizations of all kinds, he identified a recurring pattern: most people don't need more information or more advice. They need a space to think clearly, without judgment, and a concrete push to act today — not tomorrow.
founder.p3Strong: Three Billion Heartbeats is that space.
founder.p3: The answer to a question Mario has been asking himself for years: how do I help someone take the first step when they're stuck, without telling them what to do?

faq.title: What people
faq.subtitle: This page answers your doubts so you can decide whether Three Billion Heartbeats fits you. Direct answers, no marketing.
faq.notFoundPre: If what you're looking for isn't here,
faq.ctaSubtitle: You start without giving any data. The email is asked for only when there's something worth saving.

what.a: A digital AI mentor that walks with you so you understand what's going on and take the next step. It isn't a productivity app or a generic chatbot: it asks questions so you find your own answers, instead of handing you empty advice.

naming.a: A human heart beats around three billion times in a lifetime. Each beat is a choice — most of them unconscious. The project exists so that more of your beats have real direction, not to add more noise.

vsChatGPT.q: How is it different from ChatGPT or other AIs?
vsChatGPT.a: ChatGPT answers what you ask. We work the other way around: we challenge before we instruct. The mentor is trained on a specific pedagogical framework — validate the emotion, order the thinking, propose a small action — and remembers your context between conversations to truly walk with you.

noPsy.q: Do I need to know about psychology or mindfulness to use it?
noPsy.a: No. You use it by writing as you would speak to someone you trust. The mentor adapts to whatever you bring on the day.

wellState.q: Can I use it if I'm fine and just want clarity?
wellState.a: Yes. You don't need to be unwell to use it. Many people use it to decide, to clear their head before something important, or to sustain a good streak.

register.q: Do I need to register to start?
register.a: No. You enter the chat and start talking. We don't ask for an email, name, or card to try it. That's our promise: crossing the door costs nothing.

whyEmail.q: Why does it ask me for the email later?
whyEmail.a: Only when there's something worth keeping — a goal, a committed action, a conversation worth coming back to. The email saves your progress so you don't lose it if you close the browser. If you don't want to leave it, you keep using it the same way without saving.

attachAnon.q: What if I came in anonymously and now want to save what I talked about?
attachAnon.a: Yes. At any moment you can attach your session to an email and everything you've discussed gets linked to your account — without losing anything.

when.q: When does it suit me to use it?
when.a: When you feel something is off but can't name it, when you freeze in front of a decision, when you fall back into a pattern, or when you want to think out loud without feeling you're bothering anyone.

time.q: How long does it take to help me?
time.a: A single conversation can clear something up in 10 minutes. Deeper changes take longer: we usually see clear patterns from 3-4 weeks of regular use. We don't promise quick magic — we do promise accompaniment that adds up day by day.

memory.q: Does the mentor remember what I told it?
memory.a: Yes. It keeps your context between sessions: your open goals, the patterns it detects, what has worked, and what you've avoided. It doesn't make you repeat your story every time.

enneagram.q: What is the Enneagram test and what's it for?
enneagram.a: An optional 90-statement questionnaire (10-12 minutes) at /profile/eneagrama. We use it for one thing only: to tune the mentor's tone and questions to how you operate. If your type is perfectionist, it avoids "shoulds"; if you tend to avoid conflict, it asks more directly what YOU want. It doesn't label you in the chat or tell anyone. You can repeat it whenever you want.

weeklyLetter.a: Once a week the mentor writes you a short letter about what it has seen in you — quoting your own words — and ends with a single question for the coming week. It arrives by email if you turn it on; otherwise it stays in the app.

teamLetter.a: Different from the weekly letter. After a few turns in the chat, an offer appears: if you'd like, someone from the team reads your thread and writes you a personal note to your email in the following days. It's optional, not automatic, and signed by a real person — not the AI. Useful when you want a human eye on something specific you're working on.

exercises.q: Are there exercises or just conversation?
exercises.a: Both. Beyond the chat: guided breathing, daily check-ins, a journal, goal work with small actions, a free impulse test, a remaining-heartbeats calculator, and "capsules" — letters you write to your future self that get delivered on the date you choose.

structured.q: Is there a structured plan or is everything free-form?
structured.a: Both. You can talk at the pace you want. Or step into the 30-day challenge or 21-day Impulse Mode, which give you a clear sequence: a focus, a check-in, and a concrete action every day.

individual.q: Is there a community or is it only individual?
individual.a: It's individual when you enter — just you and the mentor. When you want, you can join a circle: a closed group of four people who share the same recent emotional pattern. It doesn't replace the mentor, it complements it with a peer mirror.

join.q: How do I join a circle?
join.a: There's no list to sign up to. We assign you a circle automatically when there's a match with your current state. The pairing is by pattern affinity, not by age or demographics, and it respects your anonymity inside the group.

inside.a: Each week a "pulse" opens: one question. Each member responds whenever they want during 7 days — anonymously. When it closes, the mentor leaves you a private debrief that picks up what from the group touches you. Cycles last six weeks and at the end you receive a closing letter archived forever.

whoReads.a: No one reads them by default. They're stored encrypted so the mentor keeps context. We'd only access a specific conversation if you open a support ticket and ask us to do so.

circleAnon.q: And inside the circle, do the others know who I am?
circleAnon.a: No. Replies in the circle are anonymous to other members — your name, email, and photo aren't shown. Only the content of what you write.

training.q: Do you use my data to train AI or for advertising?
training.a: No. We don't sell data, we don't share it with advertisers, and we don't use it to train third-party models. The conversations are yours.

exportDelete.q: Can I export or delete everything?
exportDelete.a: Yes. From settings you can download a full export (GDPR Art. 15) or delete your account. Deleting it also wipes the associated conversations and content.

free.q: Is it free? Is there a trial?
free.a: You can come in and try it without registering. The free test and the 30-day challenge don't require payment either. The current plans and details are on the pricing page.

pro.q: What's included in the Pro plan?
pro.a: Unlimited conversations, 21-day Impulse Mode with follow-up, challenges personalised to your pattern, access to circles, and the weekly letter by email. Current price at /precios.

cancel.q: Can I cancel whenever I want?
cancel.a: Yes. There's no lock-in. You cancel from your account and keep access until the end of the period already paid for.

pause.q: What if I want to take a break without losing what I've worked on?
pause.a: Your account and conversations are kept even if you don't come in for weeks. You return whenever you want and the mentor picks up where you left off.

mobile.a: Yes. It's an optimised web app: you use it from the mobile or desktop browser, with nothing to install.

vsTherapy.q: Does it replace a psychologist or psychiatrist?
vsTherapy.a: No, and we'll never claim it does. It's complementary accompaniment. If there's a diagnosed disorder, ongoing treatment, or a crisis, the human professional is the one who should run the case — we can support between sessions, not replace them.

crisis.q: What happens if the mentor detects I'm not well?
crisis.a: If risk appears (suicidal ideation, self-harm, acute crisis), the mentor stops doing coaching and connects you with emergency resources (988 — Suicide & Crisis Lifeline US — and 112, EU emergency). That's a line we don't cross.

trustedContact.q: Can I leave a trusted contact for extreme situations?
trustedContact.a: Yes. In settings you can register a trusted contact. If you enter a sustained crisis, the system can notify them — only in scenarios you've defined, never by default.

aiMistakes.a: Sometimes, yes. That's why the pedagogical framework is designed to give you back questions instead of closed answers: the decision is always yours. If something the mentor says doesn't fit you, say so — adjust the course in the same conversation.

team.a: Built by Startidea, a small team in Spain committed to emotional wellbeing through technology. More on the "About us" page.

languages.q: Which languages is it available in?
languages.a: Spanish natively, plus English, Portuguese (Portugal), and French on the home and main pages. Spanish is where the tone and pedagogical framework were tuned first — the other languages are being rolled out page by page.

pros.q: Is there a version for professionals or teams?
pros.a: Yes. We work with organisations and mental health professionals. More details at /para-profesionales.

howTo.title: We don't give advice.
howTo.subtitle: Most wellbeing apps try to give you more information. We work the other way around: we hand back the question you aren't asking yourself. This is the framework the mentor uses in every conversation.
howTo.lastReviewed: Reviewed by the Three Billion Heartbeats clinical team
howTo.pipelineTitle: How the mentor processes every message
howTo.pipelineSubtitle: Behind every reply there are five phases. It isn't improvisation: it's a process designed so that what we say to you makes sense here and now.

validar.title: Validate the emotion
validar.desc: Before thinking, feeling. We name what's happening inside without judgement and without rushing to fix it.

ordenar.title: Sort the thinking
ordenar.desc: We separate fact from interpretation. What happened, what you tell yourself about what happened, and what you feel about what you tell yourself.

interpelar.title: Challenge
interpelar.desc: The uncomfortable question no one is asking you. Not to judge you — so you see what you've been dodging for a while.

actuar.title: Propose action
actuar.desc: A small, concrete step, today. Not a perfect plan for next week. Real movement, not intention.

cerrar.title: Close without dependency
cerrar.desc: We end leaving you with more clarity, not more need of us. The goal is for you to need us less, not more.

howTo.principlesTitle: The principles that hold it up

interpelar.title: Challenge before instructing
interpelar.desc: A well-placed question creates more change than the best instruction. Advice is forgotten; the answer you discover yourself is not.

porque.title: Always the why
porque.desc: Acting without understanding why is obedience, not change. If you don't know what's moving you, the change won't last.

localGlobal.title: From local to global
localGlobal.desc: We start with what's concrete today — this block, this emotion — and from there we discover the larger pattern. Not the other way around.

gafas.title: New glasses
gafas.desc: What holds you back the most is usually what you've normalised. Part of the work is making you see what you no longer see.

inside.title: Change comes from within
inside.desc: No one changes because they're told to. You change when you connect with your own reason. Our job is to accompany that process, not force it.

progress.title: Progress, not perfection
progress.desc: An imperfect step today is worth more than a perfect plan tomorrow. Real movement beats good intentions.

howTo.adaptSubtitle: The mentor by default already adapts to your emotional state, your dominant pattern, and the phase you're in. If you want to go a step further, there are two options — optional — to tune the experience to how you work.

enneagram.title: Enneagram test
enneagram.desc: 90 statements in 10-12 minutes. The mentor adjusts its tone and questions to your type: with a perfectionist it avoids the «shoulds», with someone who tends to avoid conflict it asks directly what you want. It doesn't label you in the chat. It sits in your profile.

teamLetter.title: Human letter from the team
teamLetter.desc: After a few turns in the chat an offer appears: if you want, someone from the team reads your thread and writes you a personal note to your email over the following days. A real person signs it — not the AI. It's optional and you request it from the chat itself.

howTo.notDoSubtitle: So it's clear where the limits of the method are — and where a human professional begins.
howTo.notDo1: We don't diagnose disorders. That's clinical work.
howTo.notDo2: We don't prescribe treatments or medication.
howTo.notDo3: We don't replace therapy or sessions with your psychologist.
howTo.notDo4: We don't hand out empty motivational lines or magic recipes.
howTo.notDo5: We don't tell you what to do with your life.
howTo.notDo6: We don't expect you to change quickly. Real change takes time.
howTo.ctaNote: The method only makes sense when you live it.

comparison.title: Three Billion Heartbeats vs ChatGPT, therapy and wellness apps
comparison.subtitle: If you're deciding which tool to use to sort out what's going on with you, this honestly compares what each one does and when to pick which. Without inflating ours. Without hiding what we don't do.
comparison.lastUpdated: Last updated: {date} · Reviewed by the Three Billion Heartbeats clinical team.

privacy.producto: Yes — hard delete, encryption in transit, clear policy

section1.title: When to choose Three Billion Heartbeats and when to choose therapy?
section1.p1: if you have a prior clinical diagnosis, persistent suicidal ideation, severe eating disorders, untreated dependencies, suspected psychosis or complex trauma. In those cases the platform isn't enough and we'll tell you so explicitly from the chat.
section1.p2: if you're dealing with blocks, doubts, life transitions, procrastination or need a structured space to sort your thinking and move into action. Also if you already have a therapist and need support between sessions.
section1.p3: when your therapist finds it useful: many professionals work with us as structured complement between their consultations. See

section2.title: Why not just use ChatGPT or Claude?
section2.p1Strong: ChatGPT and Claude are generic assistants
section2.p1Cont: , not mentors. They answer whatever you ask: if you ask for cheap motivation, they give it; if you ask for clinical advice, they do too (and there's a real risk there). Three Billion Heartbeats has a hardcoded pedagogical framework: hollow imperatives like "you can do it" or "keep it up" are forbidden, ending in a question is mandatory, and when it detects self-harm or suicidal ideation language,
section2.p1Strong2: it stops conversing as a coach
section2.p1End: and redirects to emergency resources + alerts the clinical team.
section2.p2: On top of that, Three Billion Heartbeats remembers your emotional state across sessions, your active goals and the actions you completed or postponed. ChatGPT, by default, starts from scratch every conversation.

section3.title: What does Three Billion Heartbeats offer that Calm, Headspace or other meditation apps don't?
section3.p1: Calm and Headspace are excellent for
section3.p1Strong: guided relaxation, sleep hygiene and mindfulness practice
section3.p1Cont: . They're pre-recorded exercises you execute. There's no conversation, no tracking of your context, no action outside the meditation moment.
section3.p2: Three Billion Heartbeats does the opposite:
section3.p2Strong: structured conversation + concrete actions outside the app
section3.p2Cont: . The focus isn't lowering momentary stress, it's moving forward on what you have stuck. They're not mutually exclusive: you can use Calm to sleep better and Three Billion Heartbeats to decide whether to leave your job. They're different tools.

section4.title: Privacy and clinical supervision — what you should know
section4.item1: are processed by external AI (Anthropic Claude) under a privacy agreement with the provider.
section4.item2: on the team can access histories of users with elevated risk (protocol supervised by the responsible psychologist). This is documented in the consent when you register.
section4.item3: (TLS). There's no additional column-level encryption in the database — we recommend not sharing information you wouldn't share with a standard software provider.
section4.item4: (hard delete) available at any time from your account settings.

comparison.faqQ1: Is Three Billion Heartbeats a substitute for psychological therapy?
comparison.faqA1: No. Three Billion Heartbeats does not diagnose, does not prescribe, and does not replace a professional therapist. It's a support between sessions or a first point of contact for people who don't yet have access to therapy. It has a psychologist responsible for clinical criteria who supervises risk detection and interventions.
comparison.faqQ2: Why not just use ChatGPT or Claude?
comparison.faqA2: ChatGPT and Claude are generic assistants. Three Billion Heartbeats applies a specific pedagogical framework (question before instructing, questions before answers), detects risk language and redirects to clinical resources, remembers your emotional state across sessions, proposes concrete time-bounded actions, and is supervised by a psychology professional. ChatGPT answers anything without context; Three Billion Heartbeats accompanies a process.
comparison.faqQ3: When is a meditation app like Calm or Headspace better than Three Billion Heartbeats?
comparison.faqA3: If what you're looking for is guided relaxation, sleep hygiene or mindfulness without a personalized process, a meditation app is more direct. Three Billion Heartbeats is conversational and focuses on blocks, decisions and life transitions — it doesn't replace breathing exercises or guided meditation sessions. They can complement each other.
comparison.faqQ4: When to go to therapy instead of using Three Billion Heartbeats?
comparison.faqA4: Whenever there's a prior clinical diagnosis, persistent suicidal ideation, severe eating disorders, severe dependencies, psychosis, or suspected complex trauma. Three Billion Heartbeats can support you between sessions, but it doesn't replace professional 1:1 treatment. If you don't have a therapist and you believe you need one, Three Billion Heartbeats will explicitly suggest it.
comparison.faqQ5: What happens with my privacy? Who can read my conversations?
comparison.faqA5: Conversations are processed by external AI (Anthropic Claude via OpenRouter) under a privacy agreement. On the Three Billion Heartbeats server, the clinical role can access conversations of users with high riskLevel or active crisis as part of the clinical supervision protocol. Your data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and you can request complete erasure at any time (GDPR).

useCases.title: It depends on
useCases.subtitle: The mentor isn't the same thing for everyone. Four real ways people are using it. Look at the one that most resembles your moment.
useCases.footerNote: If you don't recognize yourself in any of them — or recognize yourself in several — it's fine. The mentor adapts to what you bring the day you come in. These are just examples, not labels.

bloqueos.title: You know something has to change, but you don't get started
bloqueos.pitch: You keep going around the same thing without moving forward. You're clear you don't want to keep going as you are, but every time you sit down to decide, another doubt shows up. It's not lack of information — it's something else.
bloqueos.signal1: You postpone important decisions "until you have it clear"
bloqueos.signal2: You consume content about the topic but don't act
bloqueos.signal3: You feel that if you get it wrong you won't be able to fix it
bloqueos.signal4: The people around you have already given you advice — it doesn't help
bloqueos.how1: The mentor separates fact from interpretation so you can see what is fear and what is judgment
bloqueos.how2: Sends back uncomfortable questions you yourself are dodging
bloqueos.how3: Proposes the smallest possible step today — not the perfect plan
bloqueos.how4: Reviews with you the patterns when the decision keeps coming back
bloqueos.limit: If the block comes with sustained depressive symptoms or disabling anxiety, complement it with a human professional.

ansiedad.title: You're racing inside even though on the outside everything works
ansiedad.pitch: It's not a diagnosed disorder. It's that knot that comes with you when you wake up, the head that won't stop, the feeling that you're always behind. You want to understand it before it escalates.
ansiedad.signal1: You find it hard to switch off even when nothing is urgent
ansiedad.signal2: You mentally review what could go wrong before going to sleep
ansiedad.signal3: You get angry at small things and then feel guilty
ansiedad.signal4: Your body warns you (tension, insomnia, digestion) and you ignore it
ansiedad.how1: Daily check-ins that force you to name what you feel before acting
ansiedad.how2: Guided breathing exercises to bring down the peak in the moment
ansiedad.how3: The mentor identifies patterns between what you think and what happens in your body
ansiedad.how4: Guided journal to separate the real threat from the imagined one
ansiedad.limit: If you have panic attacks, significant avoidances or the anxiety interferes with your daily life, this does not replace clinical assessment.

transiciones.title: You're in an "in-between". The old no longer, the new not yet
transiciones.pitch: Job change, breakup, move, end of a stage, start of another. It's not a crisis: it's the uncomfortable ground between two versions of you. You need to sort out what you're letting go and choose what you're building.
transiciones.signal1: You find it hard to explain to others how you are without sounding dramatic
transiciones.signal2: Sometimes you're fine and sometimes nostalgia or uncertainty take over
transiciones.signal3: You have big decisions to make and don't know where to make them from
transiciones.signal4: You ask yourself "who am I now?" more than usual
transiciones.how1: Goal-oriented work to ground the direction in concrete actions
transiciones.how2: The mentor helps you name what ended before forcing what comes next
transiciones.how3: Tracking emotional patterns to see the curve, not just the day
transiciones.how4: Contextual reminders to come back to yourself when you get lost in the noise
transiciones.limit: If the transition includes grief from recent loss or traumatic breakup, this companionship complements but does not replace specific therapy.

autoconocimiento.title: You're not unwell. You want to see yourself with more honesty
autoconocimiento.pitch: There's no crisis. There's curiosity. You want to understand why you react the way you do, what patterns repeat in your relationships, what values you're living and which ones you set aside. To see the glasses through which you look.
autoconocimiento.signal1: You have time and energy, but feel you could live more awake
autoconocimiento.signal2: You notice repeated patterns but don't know exactly what they are
autoconocimiento.signal3: You want to write/reflect regularly but can't sustain the habit alone
autoconocimiento.signal4: You care about how you work, not just what to do
autoconocimiento.how1: Guided journal with questions you wouldn't ask yourself alone
autoconocimiento.how2: Pattern system that returns to you what you're not seeing
autoconocimiento.how3: Deep conversations about values, decisions, relationships
autoconocimiento.how4: No rush to "fix" anything — your own pace
autoconocimiento.limit: This case has no particular contraindications beyond the general limits: the mentor accompanies, doesn't diagnose.

pricing.whyTitle: Why it's free (and for how long)
pricing.whyP1: Three Billion Heartbeats is in minimum viable product phase. It works, but it's still learning. And to learn it needs real people actually using it — not closed betas or demos no one touches.
pricing.whyP2: During these 6 months (until October 2026), the entire Pro plan is open at no cost. In exchange, your interactions help us improve the product. We don't sell your data. We don't share it. We use it, anonymized, so the tool gets better for you and for those who come next.
pricing.whyP3: When the MVP phase ends, the free plan will keep unlimited chat. Pro will be for whoever wants cross-device continuity, persistent memory between sessions and Impulse Mode. No surprises.
pricing.futureSubtitle: These will be the prices once the open-access period ends. MVP users will get special conditions.

pricing.whyProTitle: Why does the Pro plan exist?
pricing.whyProDesc: Real change doesn't happen in one conversation — it happens when you keep the thread going for weeks. Continuity is what turns an idea into a habit. Pro exists so you don't lose that thread: unlimited conversations, action tracking, and a mentor that remembers your full story.

free.a: Yes. During the MVP phase (until October 2026) there's no charge. You don't need a credit card. Just sign up with your email.

data.a: Your conversations and emotional data are processed anonymously to improve the product. They are never sold or shared with third parties. You can delete everything at any time from Settings.

afterMvp.q: What happens when the MVP ends?
afterMvp.a: You'll be able to keep using the free plan with unlimited chat, or choose Pro at its regular price for extras (cross-device continuity, persistent memory, Impulse Mode). MVP users will get special conditions.

psy.q: Does Three Billion Heartbeats replace a psychologist?
psy.a: No. It's a conversational AI mentoring tool. It helps you organize ideas and take action, but it does not replace professional therapy. In case of crisis, contact 988 or your local emergency line.

mobile.q: Can I use it from my phone?
mobile.a: Yes. The site is optimized for mobile and you can add it to your home screen. You can also use the Telegram bot to chat directly from there.
